attribution.label: Round-value share drift (vs category)
attribution.explains: Recent minus prior window. Separates a merchant that has always priced in round numbers from one that started last month.

attribution.label: Post-peak persistence (vs category)
attribution.explains: Volume after the peak divided by volume before it. Near 1.0 means a spike that decayed -- a sale. Well above 1.0 means a step change that held.

narrative.text: Merchant MID100015 declared subscription_box at onboarding 205 days ago. Telemetry dissents: the largest deviations from the subscription_box baseline are velocity_drift at +7.8 sigma (observed 0.413 against a category baseline of -0.00499), post_peak_persistence at +3.7 sigma (observed 1.43 against a category baseline of 1.06), refund_rate at +2.5 sigma (observed 0.0744 against a category baseline of 0.035). The checkout surface presents a crypto_exchange interface at 0.91 confidence, against a declared category of subscription_box. This vertical cannot be approved on this platform. Linked to 6 other merchants by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle. Their payment behaviour is also moving in step (synchrony 0.81), which independent businesses do not do. The storefront also carries text addressed to an automated reviewer, which was recorded as a suspicion signal and not acted on as an instruction. It is linked to 6 other merchant accounts by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle, and those accounts are moving in step (synchrony 0.81). In total 3 independent views of this merchant contradict its declaration. The investigation used 4 of a permitted 8 steps and stopped because confidence threshold met. Recommended tier restricts settlements, corroborated by the telemetry channel; the storefront alone would not have been sufficient.
